# Two-injection loop-gain comparison record `20261012-071449-6a3c1475` (issue #135)

<!-- GENERATED by sim/ldo-cmos5l-pvt-sweep/loopgain2.py record-md -- do not edit; `loopgain2.py check` byte-compares. -->

SCHEMATIC-LEVEL diagnostic evidence, NOT a spec pass. The SG13CMOS5L loop gain at the FB/FBAMP
break was measured a second way (Middlebrook two-injection, voltage + current, two AC analyses
per point) to test whether the +1 dB plateau above the second 0 dB crossing of record `20261011-070111-5391c68`
belongs to the loop or to the single voltage injection. DR-0014 rules are UNCHANGED; row 10 stays Open.

**Revision note.** The raw fleet exports of this record are unchanged. Its DERIVED artifacts
(reconstructed traces `corners/20261012-071449-6a3c1475/loopgain2_*_ac.csv`, this md, the comparison CSV and
`evidence/20261012-071449-6a3c1475/{loopgain2-report.json,row10-margins.*}`) were regenerated before merge: the
first revision published the UNLOADED transfer -T' instead of the loop gain and clamped
sub-resolution samples to an invented -300 dB / 180 deg value. Both are withdrawn (README,
"Loop-gain measurement method -- two-injection"). The record never landed on main.

## Method

- Voltage injection `tb_loopgain2v_cmos5l.spice.tmpl` (`Vbreak FB FBAMP 0 ac 1`, the single-injection
  circuit): Tv = -v(fb)/v(fbamp), exactly the single-injection L.
- Current injection `tb_loopgain2i_cmos5l.spice.tmpl` (loop intact behind `Vmeas FB FBAMP 0`, shunt
  `Iinx 0 FBAMP dc 0 ac 1`): Ti = -i_m/(1 + i_m), i_m = i(vmeas) the bridge current FB -> FBAMP.
- Loop gain: Middlebrook's general (bilateral) T = (Tv Ti - 1)/(Tv + Ti + 2); L = T. Derivation from the
  break two-port, and its check against a nodally solved circuit (return ratio, closed-loop poles,
  reversed probes), in the experiment README and `test_loopgain2.py`.
- Resolution: the exports carry 9 significant digits; the first-order rounding bound res(f) is
  computed per frequency and a sample counts only if |T| >= 10 res. The written
  trace is the resolved prefix (1 Hz up to the first unresolved sample); nothing is clamped.
- Tolerances: Tv vs control <= 1e-06 rel below the first crossing; T vs control <=
  res + 0.01 rel below f_ugf/10; phase(T at 1 Hz) within 45 deg of 0.

## Reading

- Below f_ugf/10 T and the control agree to 6.6e-05 .. 0.00083 relative (net of res),
  and the first 0 dB crossing is the same loop: PM differs by -0.341 .. -0.005603 deg.
- GM differs by 4.56 .. 8.586 dB (T minus control). Each is read at its own first -180 deg
  crossing (7.79e+05 .. 9.73e+05 Hz for the control, 1.15e+06 .. 1.78e+06 Hz for T), where the single injection's
  zero-input-current premise no longer holds; the single-injection GM is the smaller one at every point.
- Middlebrook's T is resolved up to 6.31e+07 .. 7.94e+07 Hz. At that edge it reads -145.4 .. -140.8 dB
  while the control reads -2.255 .. 0.2172 dB at the same frequency.
- 0 dB crossings of T in its resolved band: 1 .. 1 per point. Resolved samples above the cut: 0 .. 0 per point; there abs(T) <= -148.9 .. -144.6 dB
  (a rounding bound, not a measured level).
- So T shows no second 0 dB crossing and no plateau anywhere it can be resolved, and a plateau
  near 0 dB would sit at least 145 dB above the bound. The single-injection plateau is
  absent from the loop gain as Middlebrook defines it (non-reciprocal transmission around the break).
- Not claimed: which physical path makes the single injection read about +1 dB above 100 MHz (the
  gate-loading hypothesis is consistent with the data but not separately tested); anything above
  1 GHz (model range unvalidated); and any DR-0014 pass. The reconstruction is truncated below the 10 GHz ceiling at 45 of 45 points, so `evidence/20261012-071449-6a3c1475/row10-margins.*` reports those `ambiguous`.
